messages:
Anika (PM): Heads-up — we got three prioritized customer asks that affect GA acceptance: stricter SLA tiers, clearer pricing for burst/overage, and a short support runbook. Need owners and minimal scope to hit GA.
Devon (EngOps): I can own the SLA doc and the capacity mapping. Proposal: define two SLA tiers (Standard / Enterprise) with clear latency targets per model class.
Ravi (SRE): We should avoid a single-number SLA. Suggest we publish p50/p95/p99 latency, availability (monthly), and clear SLI definitions. Also call out degraded-mode fallback behavior.
María (Support): I'll draft the oncall playbook and runbook snippets. Need answers on expected error budgets + who does tier-1 triage vs. engineering escalation.
Lucas (FinOps): For pricing, customers want predictable burst rules. Can we define burst buckets and overage multipliers? Also need example TCO for 100k vs 1M requests.
Anika (PM): Good. For GA checklist, let's keep minimal: SLA doc, published pricing example sheet, basic runbook, alerts+dashboards, and an owners table. Also require a canary plan + rollback criteria.
Devon (EngOps): Can we carve the SLA by model sizes: small (<=4B), medium (4-30B), large (>30B)? Each gets a p95 latency target and supporting cost guidance. I'll produce a table by EOD Thu.
Ravi (SRE): For alerts: we need SLO burn rate alert at 1.5x, and critical when 3x. Instrument token-level latency histograms, and a prefix cache hit metric. I'll add panel suggestions for Console.
María (Support): Runbook needs quick checks: 1) is model routing healthy? 2) is cache warm? 3) any recent deploys? Include short canned replies for customers. I'll add example phrasing.
Anika (PM): Customer asks also want a commitment window for Dedicated capacity. Can someone confirm default reserved capacity SLA and the minimum lead time?
Devon (EngOps): Default reserved lead time is 72 hours for burst-capacity changes, and 14 days for contract-backed Dedicated. I'll put those in pricing doc draft.
Lucas (FinOps): Pricing examples: I'll add a 'what-if' calc and a short table showing marginal cost per 1k tokens with and without prefix caching. Need Devon numbers for batching assumptions.
Ravi (SRE): Note: p99 for >30B models on GPU-backed dedicated can be variable. We should have an explicit 'SLA exceptions' section listing model classes where latency targets are best-effort with fallback to throughput SLOs.
Anika (PM): Owners: SLA -> Devon, Support runbook -> María, Pricing examples -> Lucas, Telemetry/alerts -> Ravi. I'll track dependencies and publish an owner matrix.
Devon (EngOps): Quick checklist snippet for GA README: ```- SLA doc published - Pricing sheet published - Support runbook linked - Console dashboards live - Canary run (1000 reqs/min) - Rollback plan documented```
María (Support): I'll prep a 1-pager for CSMs with canned responses and escalation steps.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/2026-03-18T15:05Z
Ravi (SRE): Noted — avoid major infra changes during canary window. If we see >2% error spike hold rollout.
Anika (PM): Risk register quick notes: a) dedic capacity forecasting errors, b) SLA expectations mismatch for big models, c) pricing surprise for bursty customers. Need mitigations.
Devon (EngOps): Mitigations: billing cap guardrail, model-specific best-effort disclaimers, and a one-click capacity throttle in Console.
Lucas (FinOps): I'll add example invoices and a short 'how to read your bill' section to the pricing sheet.
Anika (PM): Timeline: SLA/pricing/runbook drafts by Fri COB, dashboards + canary by Mon, GA decision Wed. If anything slips, we'll escalate to exec review.
María (Support): A quick question — who signs off on final SLA wording? Legal or Product?
Anika (PM): Product + Legal for wording, Ops for feasibility.
Devon (EngOps): I'll post the SLA draft in product channel when ready.
Ravi (SRE): I'll push alert dashboards to staging and share links.
Lucas (FinOps): Added initial pricing spreadsheet link: https://redwood.app/sheets/pricing-ga-draft (internal)
Anika (PM): Thanks team. Let's aim to keep GA scope deliberately small and measurable.
